title: Grateful Dead Live at Stadium, U.C Santa Barbara on 1973-05-20
lineage: 7in Master Reels at 7.5ips half-track > Panasonic SV-3700 DAT > Panasonic SV-3800 DAT > DAT > CD > Samsung SW-232B extraction (EAC v0.9 beta 4) > tracking (CD Wave) > sector boundary verification (shntool v1.01) > .shn

ai_review.summary: An excellent patched soundboard captures a stellar 1973 UCSB show with blistering Here Comes Sunshine, Row Jimmy and an epic Truckin → Other One sequence.
ai_review.review: The patched SBD recording is crystal‑clear overall, with only a brief high‑frequency buzz in the first set that disappears later. Musically the concert is a tour‑de‑force – Jerry’s voice is a little strained but his guitar shines, Phil’s bass drives the band, and the group delivers standout performances of Here Comes Sunshine, Row Jimmy, Eyes, Looks Like Rain and a spectacular Truckin→Other One→Eyes→Stella Blue→Sugar Magnolia run. The set flows beautifully from a relaxed first set into an inspired second and a magical third set that truly “has wings.”

ai_rating.rationale: Consistently 4‑5 star reviews praising both the musical performance and the high‑quality patched soundboard, with only minor technical quirks.

recording_quality.technical_notes: Crisp, well‑balanced mix; occasional high‑frequency buzz (likely bass) in the first set that fades after the opening songs. Patched seamlessly, making the tape highly listenable.

standout_songs: China Cat Sunflower > I Know You Rider
show_quality.setlist_flow: A long, well‑structured concert that builds from a relaxed first set into an inspired second and a soaring third set (the “wings”), with seamless transitions and high energy throughout.

band_member_comments.Jerry: Voice sounds slightly strained/colder than usual but his guitar work remains fiery; vocals praised by several reviewers.
band_member_comments.Phil: A brief high‑frequency buzz in the first set is attributed to Phil’s bass (big brown) by one reviewer.
